clue.text: 2 or 7, what's around 13 or 3, 4 or 25 — all standard

parts.note: the answers to 2 Down (a Leninist) and 7 Down (claret) can both be called red: the political colour and the wine
the white of the eye surrounds the iris of 13 Across, and pale (3 Down) can mean whitish
all gathers the three colours into one list, which in the usual phrase is joined by and
to blue money is to squander it, as in 4 Down, and blue also means smutty, like the answer to 25 Down

explanation.surface: A puzzle-wide cross-reference clue gathering colours from other answers into one flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pair of cross-references yields one colour; 'all' collects the three into the familiar phrase with AND before the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Flag, Britain's national banner or standard, is coloured in those three hues, so the phrase describes that standard.

clue.text: Revolutionary holding a number up inside border

indicators.note: inside says the turned number sits within the word for border

parts.note: a list is an old word for a border or edge of cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word nine is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A rebel keeps a number upside down within a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is a link here: the revolutionary holds the views the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Lenin is by definition a Marxist revolutionary.

clue.text: Under pressure, drink — don't go beyond this limit!

indicators.note: in this down clue the drink sits under the pressure letter, so P comes first

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A warning to a drinker under strain not to go past the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'beyond the pale', the fenced boundary once marking English-controlled land around Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a boundary fence, and going beyond it means overstepping acceptable limits.

clue.text: Handle money badly as girl and finish without penny

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the girl and finish words go round the penny letter

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl or young woman
an end is a finish
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Spending foolishly like a girl who ends up with no pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money wastefully or unwisely is to manage it poorly.

clue.text: Family man briefly seen with a daughter — barely so

indicators.note: briefly means the relative's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a male relative
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A relative turns up with his daughter, scarcely dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely so' means in a bare state, i.e. naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without clothes is being bare, which is exactly what the definition describes.

clue.text: They monitor recreational activity for Americans

definitions.meaning: people who inspect or verify things
the American name for the board game the British call draughts

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for the board game Americans call by the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors verify work, and the US name for draughts is the same plural word.

clue.text: Musical instrument missing in Bordeaux

indicators.note: missing says the word in is taken out of the instrument

parts.note: a clarinet is a woodwind instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instrument has gone astray in the French city of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the instrument in Bordeaux, but it is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the traditional British name for red wine from the Bordeaux region.

clue.text: Start of final statement in court, including 6 or 10, 21 or 22, 24 or 26

definitions.text: Start of final statement in court

parts.note: checkers (6 Down) and halma (10 Across) are both games
intent (21 Down) can mean set, as in set on something, and laid (22 Across) can mean set, as a table is
including means together with, so it stands for the and that joins the last two words of the phrase
a replica (24 Across) is a match for the original, and a union (26 Across) is a match or marriage

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue assembling the umpire's words from other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pair of references gives one word; 'including' supplies the AND. The tennis umpire's announcement at the end of a match begins with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end of a tennis match on court, the umpire's announcement opens with these words before naming the winner.

clue.text: One side of the house in ecstasy about electoral vote, initially

indicators.note: about says the joy word goes round those initials

parts.note: elation is great joy, ecstasy

indicators.note: initially means take the first letters of the two words that come before it

explanation.surface: A voter delights in casting a ballot, with electoral talk at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'about' puts EV (from 'electoral vote, initially') into ELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation in architecture is a drawing or view of one face of a building.

clue.text: Quartet can play it as part of triumphal march

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A string quartet can perform it as a section of a victory march.
explanation.walkthrough: The quartet is not musicians but four players: the board game can be played by two or four.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game for two or four players, so a group of four can play it.

clue.text: Staff in restaurant serves drink around one

indicators.note: around says the drink-giving word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to water animals is to give them drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A restaurant employee pours drinks for a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: People who serve tables are the dining-room staff of a restaurant.

clue.text: Pike mostly associated with one lake or another

indicators.note: mostly means the fish's name loses its final letter

parts.note: luce is an old name for the pike fish
another lake: Lough Erne in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An angler links a pike to one lake or the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a lake in central Switzerland, also called Lake Lucerne.

clue.text: Name of girl, like Bridget without husband

indicators.note: without says the husband letter is dropped

parts.note: Bridget is a typically Irish name

explanation.surface: A girl's name, Irish like Bridget, with no husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female first name, also that of a Greek goddess.

clue.text: Not quick to get angry — it's a harmless bloomer

parts.note: the quick are the living, so not quick means lifeless
nettle means to irritate or anger

explanation.surface: A slow-tempered person makes a blunder that does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant; this plant looks like a nettle but does not sting.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering plant resembles a stinging nettle but has no stinging hairs, so it is harmless.

clue.text: English bible, partly decorated, was attractive

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is part of the Bible
iced as a cake is decorated

explanation.surface: An ornate English Bible proved alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure, so something that enticed drew people in and exerted attraction.

clue.text: Fashion centre housing old and new fabric

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion house displays old and new textiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion centre' looks like a design hub; 'housing' says O and N go into CENTRE before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy cotton cloth with printed patterns, used for upholstery.

clue.text: Cosmetic old lady used to cover up a blemish

parts.note: ma is informal for mother, one's old lady
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: An old woman applies make-up to hide a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs MA, SCAR, A; 'used to cover up' completes the surface of a cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to the eyelashes.

clue.text: They catch people with slogan and added comment

parts.note: a mantra is a repeated slogan
PS, postscript, is a comment added to a letter

explanation.surface: Campaigners catch people with a catchphrase and a footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps for catching trespassers or poachers are made for people rather than animals.

clue.text: Middle East experts again entering area with deserts

indicators.note: entering says the again word goes into the deserts word

parts.note: to rat is to desert, so rats means deserts
bis is Latin for twice, used to mean again

explanation.surface: Specialists in the Middle East return to an area of deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' looks like sandy wastes but is the verb: rats on.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars of Arabic language and culture are specialists in the Arab Middle East.

clue.text: Some Europeans setting out in snow gear

indicators.note: setting out means arranging the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Travellers depart dressed for snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Norway are Scandinavians and so a group of Europeans.

clue.text: Inexperienced soldier that's falling beneath castle

indicators.note: in a down clue the that-is letters drop below the chess piece, so they come after it

parts.note: castle is another name for the rook in chess
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A young recruit falls below a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a raw recruit, a newcomer with little experience.

clue.text: Absorbed, like audience at circus

definitions.meaning: a circus audience sits in a big tent

explanation.definitionFit: Being wholly focused is intent, and a circus crowd is in the tent.

clue.text: How egg is produced and hatched

definitions.meaning: a hen produces an egg by laying it
hatched as a plot is devised

explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are laid by a hen, and a scheme that has been hatched has been laid.

clue.text: Resign about pound's rapid deflation

indicators.note: about says the resign phrase goes round the pound letter

parts.note: to bow out is to resign or withdraw
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A slump in the pound forces someone to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deflation' looks economic, but it means a tyre going flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre burst, its sudden loss of air, is a sudden deflation.

clue.text: Page in article left with one copy

indicators.note: in says the page letter goes inside the left-over object

parts.note: a relic is an object left over from the past
a means one

explanation.surface: A page in an article left behind, together with a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy of something.

clue.text: It's intended to arouse an extreme of passion

indicators.note: extreme points to an end letter of the word passion, here its opening one

parts.note: an extreme here means either extreme, one or the other, so the joining word is or

indicators.note: of passion, read with the extreme, also points to the closing end letter of that word

explanation.surface: Something designed to stir up great passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an extreme of passion' is either end of PASSION: P or N, run together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pornography is material created to cause sexual excitement.

clue.text: Facility for students a small number in university backed

parts.note: uni is informal for university

indicators.note: backed means the short number is written backwards

parts.note: No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A small number at university back a student facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals the abbreviated form; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A students' union is the society and building providing student services.

clue.text: Rattled in pitcher, like some stones

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Something shaken about in a jug, like stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is with an I; the grid's E form does not fit the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephritic relates to the kidneys, so kidney stones are of this kind.
